baer-heitev/3:_: Surrounding [margin]. The same applies to everything; therefore it requires that its lines be equal. Magen Avraham there; and see in responsum of Maharam Mintz and in Knesset HaGedolah on laws of writing the megillah.
baer-heitev/8:_: In a congregation. And every ten is called a congregation. Tur.
baer-heitev/9:_: Vocalization. And if there is no one who knows to read with cantillation by heart, it is permitted to write the cantillation in the megillah and to bless on it — Beer Sheva daf 109. And Magen Avraham wrote; nevertheless it appears to me that if there are no cantillation marks in the megillah it is permitted to read without cantillation, as written siman 142.
beer-hagolah/1:ה: Tur in the name of Rambam
beer-hagolah/2:ב: Tur in the name of Rambam
beer-hagolah/2:ה: Tur in the name of Rabbenu Tam
beer-hagolah/3:ב: Tur in the name of Yerushalmi
beer-hagolah/4:ב: Tur in the name of Yerushalmi
beur-hagra/11:_: Seif 11 — if. As with shofar they said in Yerushalmi Sukkah ch. 3: what is the difference between shofar, etc. — here with his voice he fulfills; and there is a voice forbidden in a building — see there.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And if he wrote it [with other materials]. And likewise in a Torah scroll — one should not infer that each alone invalidates; kankantom in the Mishnah implies it is not [valid] ink, and the same for a Torah scroll as in Shabbat 103b: if he wrote not with ink, etc. And in Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 1 halacha 11 they must write with ink; and afatzim water implies in Gittin 19a it is not ink except when both are together — then it is ink — and it teaches us that even if it is not erased as in Eruvin 13a, nevertheless it is permitted; and he ruled like R' Yehudah from R' Meir who said to each one throw in, etc., as in Laws of Tefillin ch. 1 — and this is their language: how is ink made? They gather smoke of oils, etc., soak it in afatzim water and the like and write with it that if erased it would erase — and that is the ink of optimal mitzvah to write a Torah scroll with. And if he wrote all three in afatzim water and kankantom that stands and is not erased — they are valid. If so, what did the halacha transmitted to Moshe at Sinai exclude — that they be written in ink — to exclude other dye types such as red and green and the like; that if he wrote in a Torah scroll even one letter in other dye types or in gold — these are invalid. And so wrote the Rosh in small halakhot. And this is what he says here: he wrote in other [materials], etc. And this is his language in his commentary on Sotah ch. 2: I saw in Eretz Yisrael they distance Torah scroll writing with one ink type called in Arabic chibur — only real ink; and here he erred in pesak halacha from the gemara, for the last thing said in the gemara on this matter: each throws in kankantom except the sota parsha in the Temple; and the copyist there said: as copyist I saw to explain what is chibur — as the Geonim explained: chibur is afatzim ink and they throw kankantom into it, a type of blackening earth that is not erased; and so wrote R' Chananel, etc. — see there.
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And some say it requires [processing lishmah]. This is Rabbenu Tam's view as he wrote in Menachot there, in the passage beginning "until," etc. Rabbenu Tam says halacha is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel as the sugya of damages follows him; and that in the chapter "the judgment was finished" where Abbaye and Rava disagree, etc. — Rabbenu Tam and R' Chananel explained Rava like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who requires processing lishmah; and perforce invitation is not a thing — for if not, it would be possible with skin cutting and small repairs, etc.; and so he wrote in Sanhedrin there — see there; and so he ruled regarding mezuzah; and see siman 32 and Yoreh Deah siman 288.
beur-hagra/2:ט: (ט) And regarding missing and extra [letters]. Menachot there; and see Tosafot there, passage beginning "but extra," etc.; and as written 29a, 34a — even a tip of yud; and Ran Megillah ch. 2.
beur-hagra/2:י: (י) Also required [to utter orally]. Megillah 18b: let us find support for him, etc.; baraita: R' Shimon ben Elazar said, etc. And in Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 4 halacha 1 — R' Zeira in name of Rav Chananel: even one expert in Torah like Ezra should not review from his mouth and read, as in Bereishit, etc.; and it was taught: incident of R' Meir who was in Asia and there was no megillah written in Hebrew and he reviewed from his mouth and read — we do not learn from a time of duress. And some say two writings: he wrote the first from his mouth and wrote the second from the first and hid the first and read from the second.
beur-hagra/2:כ: (כ) And to utter every word, etc. Menachot 30a; and see there Tosafot s.v. and Moshe, etc.; and so Mordekhai Laws of Megillah siman 457 — from here one can prove a Torah scroll scribe must utter with his mouth, etc.; and so all poskim; and likewise in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 274 seif 2 — and it implies that even if he writes from a written copy — for 98 cannot write it not from a written copy; and what is written siman 32 seif 31: if he is not, etc. — tefillin is different; and Magen Avraham there; and this is R' Yeshaya's view who inferred from Semag's language: it is forbidden for another person to prompt the scribe unless he returns, etc.; and one could say for emphasis he cited it even though when another prompts him he need not err as in blessing of kohanim — nevertheless it is required as we find with Moshe: even though the Holy One blessed be He speaks, nevertheless Moshe returns and speaks; and so all poskim who did not divide; and a Torah scroll requires from a written copy even though a Torah scroll requires from a written copy.
beur-hagra/2:מ: (מ) And it requires [a pole and blank], etc. Bava Batra 13b; and see there Tosafot s.v. and makes. It appears to R' Yitzchak we read: and makes at its head for surrounding and at its end to roll a pole; and so emended the Geonim there 14a: all books roll to their beginning; and there 14b: Ezra's book rolls to its beginning; and Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 1 halacha 11: they make a pole for a book at its end — for Torah from here and from here; therefore the book rolls to its beginning and Torah to its middle; and so in Mishneh Torah ch. 2 and Yadim ch. 3: R' Yishmael — at the end it is not tamei until a pole is made; and see R' Shimon there and the Rosh; and even to Rashba who upholds the reading "books" and distinguishes between glued, etc. — he admits regarding books alone one makes a pole at its end, etc.
beur-hagra/2:נ: (נ) And some say it needs tagin and some say not, etc. Ran ch. 2; and the first reasoning holds it is a matter of the body and its law is like a Torah scroll as above; and the last reasoning holds tagin are not from the body of writing as in Menachot they found for the Holy One blessed be He tied crowns, etc. — see there; and anything not of the body does not impede; and we do not say it is called a book since one must learn from writing in a scroll, etc. — from gezeirah shavah of ketivah ketivah and not learn from sefer; and see Ran and Rashba; but in Shabbat 104 that without adornments it is not letters at all; and Ran; and Mordekhai Padua; and see what is written siman 35 seif 3.
beur-hagra/3:א: (א) Seif 3 — if he divided above the writing, etc. Tur's language and per Rashi there and Ran and Mordekhai there.
beur-hagra/3:ב: (ב) And if not. Yerushalmi ch. 3 halacha 8: ten sons of Haman and kings of Canaan, etc. — for a mitzvah or to impede, etc. R' Ba bar Zavda passed and they asked him and he said in name of Rav: to impede.
beur-hagra/4:א: (א) Seif 4 — must extend. Tur's language; and it implies from their words like the first language in its writing since it is written in this siman in laws of writing.
beur-hagra/4:ג: (ג) And requires, etc. Yerushalmi there: R' Yirmiyah bar Bun — must be ish at the head of the page and et at its end — swayed and descended like this beam — meaning like two beams of a pocket equal on both sides like builders' balance; and see in Mishneh Torah there. And what is written at the head of the page means at the head of the line and at the end of the line — not as some explain at the head of the column, for otherwise why would R' Yirmiyah add after R' Yirmiyah in name of Rav who said there ten sons of Haman, etc., and song of 48, etc., one column above, etc. From this is drawn what they write ten sons of Haman in a column by itself in large letters. And the confusion is that we were not given to write ten sons of Haman in large script letters; rather the main point of what is written at the head of the page is at the head of the line as above. And R' Yirmiyah himself teaches: if from R' Yirmiyah in name of Rav one would say since ten sons of Haman were separated from all songs and equated to the song of 48 — for the matter that both are written alone one column above, etc. as above and as in the gemara — if so we would equate them entirely not to write within ten sons of Haman the word before it as in the song of kings of Canaan that begins "king," etc.; and this is what R' Yirmiyah said: must, etc., ish at the head, etc., and as above at head of line and end of line like pocket eye and two beams as above and like other megillah letters.
beur-hagra/6:ב: (ב) And if there are none [sinews], etc. As in Bava Batra 162b: supports, etc.; do not wonder, etc. Mordekhai and Hagahot Maimoniot ch. 2 s.k. 60 — reason: it must be entirely hollowed from head to end that it be one book alone except the sewing margin as in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 275 seif 1; and as in Gittin 60a: a book lacking even, etc.; and Rosh explained no sewing with it; and as written there seif 4; and Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 3: sewing halacha 11; and so Rambam Megillah ch. 2: the megillah must be sewn entirely until all its hides are one megillah.
beur-hagra/8:א: (א) Seif 8 — he did not fulfill. There; and so Rif, Rambam, Rosh, and Tur — unlike Ran.
beur-hagra/8:ב: (ב) But the individual, etc. Rambam; but Rif, Rosh, and Tur wrote he fulfills.
biur-halacha/8:ב: The individual reads from it — implies even l'chatchila even if he has a megillah written alone and can read from this [Peri Megadim]; but Rif, Rosh, and Tur wrote he fulfills [Biur HaGra].
chokhmat-shlomo/3:_: (there seif 8) One does not read in congregation from a megillah written among the Writings, etc. NB: thus is Rambam's language Megillah ch. 2 and Tur's language: if the individual read, etc. And it appears their words contradict: from "one does not read in congregation" perforce the intent is to discharge the many — yotzei; if so it implies that whoever is not congregation, even nine and one reads for all — valid; and afterward they wrote but the individual reads and fulfills yotzei — implies specifically the reader himself fulfills yotzei but to discharge his fellow even not in congregation it does not help — these contradict. In Rambam and Shulchan Aruch one could explain: since they wrote but the individual reads — implies even l'chatchila; if so one can say three distinctions: in congregation even b'dieved he does not fulfill; individual for himself reads l'chatchila; individual to discharge others initially he should not read lest we decree because of congregation, but b'dieved he fulfills since they are not congregation. But this fits Rambam who holds individual reads l'chatchila. But what of Tur who wrote: if it was bound with them and the individual read — he fulfilled — he used b'dieved language implying l'chatchila even the individual alone does not fulfill; if so his words contradict: first he wrote individual reads implying specifically for himself but not to discharge his fellow, and afterward only congregation implying in individuality one discharges, etc. — requires study. What seemed to me to settle this: from here will be proven what Magen Avraham disputes above siman 689 s.k. 10 whether one individual discharges his fellow even if expert or specifically if not expert but expert does not discharge — see there. From here will be proven Tur also holds one does not discharge his fellow if he is expert. Per this one can explain. In Yerushalmi ch. 2 halacha 4: R' Chelbo, etc. — if written in chumashim one does not read in rabim; R' Tanchuma said: because of amateurs — till here. Knesset HaGedolah strained there: amateurs means they will say it is exempt, etc. — see there — strained; especially per Ran's explanation it is only from honor of congregation — certainly not Knesset HaGedolah's intent. In my humble opinion the intent is thus: in our Talmud the reading is "congregation" but Yerushalmi says "rabim." Congregation per Beit HaLevi is specifically in synagogue; Tur wrote every ten is called congregation but less than ten all agree not called congregation; but rabim even three are called rabim as known in Nedarim 34b and many places. Therefore Yerushalmi teaches even with less than ten only in rabim one does not read. Therefore it was hard: it implies if not written in chumashim permitted in rabim — yet one does not discharge his fellow with less than ten; and if dealing with ten should have said congregation — therefore he says because of amateurs who are not expert to read — by this the individual discharges his fellow — therefore teaches in any case if written among Writings he does not fulfill. Also intent simply: in Talmud it says a foreigner who heard Assyrian fulfills and challenges he did not know what is said and answers like men and am ha'aretz; afterward: are the Achashteranim sons of the Ramachim known to us — only mitzvah of reading and publicizing miracle; so too one who does not understand fulfills only from reading and publicizing miracle. Therefore Yerushalmi said because of amateurs — certainly those who understand the language since they hear it is megillah fulfill even in chumashim; only because of those who do not understand who fulfill only from reading and publicizing miracle. This fits if they see recognition; but if no recognition there is no knowledge — if so both explanations exist; and Rambam, Tur, and Shulchan Aruch hold: in congregation even if all know and understand nevertheless they do not fulfill in writing among Writings; and individual reading for himself who is the reader — if so knows from here how to read — therefore fulfills even if he does not know the language; but to discharge others with less than ten — if they are not expert even with less than ten they do not fulfill since they do not understand — no publicizing miracle; and if with ten they understand — nevertheless if written alone one does not discharge his fellow with less than ten when he is expert. Therefore Rambam, Tur, and Shulchan Aruch did not cite from either side. This fits me better than answer one: difficult they should explain b'dieved discharges in writing among Writings and not l'chatchila; but per what I said now there is no either/or and proven from all one does not discharge his fellow with less than ten only if not expert — understand and examine well.
eliyah-rabbah/10:_: [י] In chumash, etc. This is Magen Avraham's language specifically when made in a roll; but in our chumashim for everyone he did not fulfill (Bach) — till here. In my humble opinion clear from Bach itself: nevertheless they read it since there is no blessing; but he should have brought Bach's words on what Rama wrote afterward; and see above siman 649, etc., if they bless, etc. — implies per those who say they bless — same law in chumash specifically when rolled; but in our chumash for everyone they do not bless; but requires study: what is different from apples and pomegranates they do not take even without etrog; and even without blessing as end of siman 649 — one can distinguish.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [ב] To utter every word, etc. Magen Avraham challenged: behold must write from written copy — then no need to utter from mouth as siman 32 seif 31 — no difficulty: that itself above regarding tefillin that is fluent in mouth is what does not require uttering from mouth. Also it appears to me: we require specifically from written copy but not that another prompted him by heart; but Magen Avraham wrote after another prompted by heart and he writes. Requires study also Yerushalmi Ran brought there — at first glance does not imply permitted to write megillah from megillah written by heart.
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [ג] Open [parashiyot] invalid, etc. In Rama's responsum he doubts this and it seems to me to rely in time of duress (Magen Avraham), and he was not precise — it is explained there he asked this of Maharai and in Piskei Maharai siman 23 he answered invalid; nevertheless Maharai wrote there are lenient who hold not all Torah scroll law applies to megillah — requires study on Rama. And in responsum Maharam Mintz siman 61 he wrote some closed some open — what he listed there does not refer to our megillot and nuschaot.
eliyah-rabbah/9:_: [ט] Must extend, etc. It appears all this is valid b'dieved (Magen Avraham), and it implies the same law for ish at head of page in seif 3, etc., since I saw scribes in megillah writing — I exerted myself and examined responsum Maharam Mintz who brought correction of R' Aviyah and Knesset HaGedolah who brought many things contradicting the correction mentioned above; what is agreed I wrote anonymously and disputed matters I wrote in our correction. In R' Aviyah's correction: Charvona with hei; in ours with alef — first Charvona with hei and second with hei; Tam'an hamalka and Vashti with vav; asher lo tavo and Vashti with vav — in ours missing vav; hagola in R' Aviyah full vav — in ours missing vav; amen et hadassah missing vav; menoteha latet lah in R' Aviyah without vav and yud — in ours full vav missing yud — some scrolls full both; yeshnah without yud; in R' Aviyah et na'aroteyah without vav — in ours full vav; behagia tar tarveihu missing vav; lishloach yad bamelech Achashverosh missing vav in second Achashverosh; bechol malchut Achashverosh full vav; vedateihem shanot missing first vav; ve'am ve'am kelashono in R' Aviyah missing vav — Knesset HaGedolah wondered if explanation requires ve'am ve'am — then all books wrote ve'am ve'am; if intent kelashono missing vav after shin alone cannot say missing in plural language — then all books full — till here. In my humble opinion his intent: written in the book in megillah ve'am ve'am kelashono; beshem hamelech Achashverosh full vav — some books missing vav; veheyot atidim in R' Aviyah missing first yud since tavo cannot be full vav; vetavo'na full vav; el rechov in R' Aviyah missing vav — in ours full; ve'al tochelu ve'al tishtu all with vav; vayitapek Haman vayavo full vav; ki im oti vav defective; yoshev full vav; ve'lo ketiv hayoshev — Sefer Hazichronot in R' Aviyah missing final vav — in ours opposite missing first vav; lechatzer beit hamelech hachitzonah in R' Aviyah missing vav — some books full; tzorer missing vav; hayehudim in two yuds; vayikreu sofrei hamelech missing vav; asher hechelot lenofol in R' Aviyah full vav — in ours lenofel missing vav; gavoah chamishim missing vav; talahu missing vav; ba'et hahi with yud; asher mehodu missing vav; velihyot hayehudim in R' Aviyah one yud — in ours two yuds; atidim first yud tag like this — so in R' Aviyah; but I examined megillot and precise chumashim: written atudim and under first yud written vav; and though margin says atidim keri — nevertheless written with yud — requires study on Knesset HaGedolah who did not note this; yatzu mevohalim missing vav; vesason first missing vav second full; vehafach hu full vav; ha'ish Mordechai holech full vav; ve'et Ardei missing yud; tzorer missing vav; umishloach manot written twice manot — both full mishloach — some missing both — some first full some second full; matanot laevyonim in R' Aviyah missing vav — some full; asher katav Mordechai aleihem vehipil pur hu hagoral uvava lifnei hamelech all missing vav; divrei tzomet veza'akatam ume'amar Esther kim divrei hapurim veratuy lerov echav full vav — in our nuschaot hapurim missing vav — requires study in R' Aviyah's correction; Parshendata small alef; Parmashta large alef — some say opposite; I saw in megillot and nuschaot no change in alef in both; also Parshendata small tav; Parmashta small shin; Vaizata large vav small zayin — requires study in R' Aviyah; vayomer mimachan mimuchan keri; vekibel ketiv vekibelu keri.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (א) [Seif 1] One does not write the megillah, etc. — all laws of megillah writing belonging to this siman are written in Kol Yaakov part 5 stumot on this siman — we took from there.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (ג) There in Hagahah. And if they bless on it see above siman 649 regarding stolen lulav. So read. Levush. And so in printed Shulchan Aruch with Be'er Heitev.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (ד) There in Hagahah. See above siman 649, etc., seif 1 there Shulchan Aruch ruled not to bless — yotzei; and in our words lishmah b'siyata dishmaya.
kol-yaakov/10:_: (י) There in Hagahah: also must write from written copy, etc. — if he wrote not from written copy he does not fulfill except in time of duress — Darkei Moshe Erkhin letter 9, Malbim kelal 24 letter 2 in Chochmah, Beit Yosef in laws of megillah writing letter 8; but permitted to copy megillah from that written copy by heart — Eliyah Rabbah s.k. 2, Malbim there; and see Biur HaGra letter 15 who wrote in name of Yerushalmi megillah and brought Biur HaGra: if after copying he buries the written-by-heart copy — and specifically if on hide but if on paper need not bury — see above letter 3.
kol-yaakov/3:_: (ג) Printed megillah invalid. Bach, Peri Chadash letter 2, Eliyah Rabbah letter 5, Knesset HaGedolah siman 21 letter 7, in Lechem Hapanim Shaarei Ephraim shaar 6 letter 59. And if they already printed megillah on parchment must bury it — for one who sees them on parchment in form of written megillot will think they are valid and read them and not fulfill yotzei and bless in vain. But to print them on paper is permitted — they will not err. Birkei Yosef part 1 siman 7 letter 40 in laws of megillah writing letter 18; and see our words Yoreh Deah siman 271 letter 24.
kol-yaakov/4:_: (ד) There: requires scoring, etc., and must score every line like a Torah scroll. Darkei Moshe letter 1, Magen Avraham letter 1, Eliyah Rabbah letter 1, Chayei Adam kelal 155 letter 10, Malbim kelal 24 letter 1 in Chochmah and letter 3 in Binah. And see Erkhin letter 4 who wrote thus is Maran's view; and so in Beit Yosef letter 3; and so in Sefer Hakavanot shaar 6 in Purim derush 1 — law like Torah scroll; explained in Pa'at Hasadeh shaar 28 Tikkunei Purim ch. 6 regarding scoring and tagin; and so practiced here in Baghdad to score all lines like Torah scroll. And if he did not score all lines even b'dieved invalid — Knesset HaGedolah there in Malbim Binah; and if he has no scored megillah but only chumash — Beit Yosef wrote he reads but does not bless; and when he obtains a scored megillah he returns and reads with blessing since majority poskim hold megillah not entirely scored is invalid; and if when he returns he reads from valid megillah he will not want to bless lest Orach Chayyim and Levush who hold chumash suffices not leave him — end. But it appears he should not bless — Zechor LeAvraham part 1 halacha 2 letter 60 and part 3 letter 60: for seif 2 to be lenient we do not follow majority; and even if doubt is only in blessing not in mitzvah performance — nevertheless do not bless; and so Darkei Adam siman 15 or 18.
kol-yaakov/5:_: (ה) There: its hide does not require processing lishmah, etc. Acharonim wrote not to rely on this reasoning except in time of duress when he has no other megillah and not to bless on it — Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham letter 2, Malbim kelal 24 letter 1 in Chochmah letter 2 in Binah; and so Rokeach letter 1 for halacha like Yeshu'at Yaakov; Knesset HaGedolah siman 28 letter 1 — unlike Beit Yosef letter 4. And so practiced here in Baghdad to process megillah hide lishmah.
kol-yaakov/7:_: (ז) Its law like Torah scroll, etc. — the same for line count and column width to write "for your families" and between line to line a full line and between word to word a full small letter and margin above three fingerbreadths and below four and between page to page full width of two fingerbreadths and its lines equal — Hagahot Maimoniot ch. 2 Laws of Megillah letter 50, Magen Avraham letter 3, Eliyah Rabbah letter 1, Chayei Adam kelal 155 letter 10, Malbim kelal 24 letter 8 in Chochmah; and some say not exacting on line count — Knesset HaGedolah siman 28 letter 4 in Lechem Hapanim; and in any case not less than eleven lines for ish at head of page and ten at end of page — Malbim there Binah letter 4; and some say when we learn megillah from Torah scroll we mean matters invalidating Torah scroll but matters not invalidating Torah such as line length regarding pages, etc. — in megillah valid even l'chatchila — Ma'aseh Rokeach on Rambam ch. 1 Laws of Megillah 49 on seif 2 s.v. and know Erkhin letter 8, Zera Emet part 1 siman 100; on this they rely here in Baghdad not to be exacting on margin above below between pages line count and hide measure to make like Torah scroll — for all these do not invalidate Torah scroll b'dieved; see Yoreh Deah siman 273 seif 5 and Taz siman 272 s.k. 4.
kol-yaakov/8:_: (ח) There: its law like Torah scroll, etc. — megillah that on last page wrote only three or four lines and the rest a section and also did not finish in middle of line only at end — valid to read l'chatchila — Zera Emet part 1 siman 100, Machberet, Erkhin letter 8, Sha'arei Chayyim letter 56, Malbim kelal 24 letter 10 in Binah, Amudei Mishneh kelal 22 letter 3, Beit Yosef letter 14; and what Zera Emet wrote at end of siman and brought in Beit Yosef: if impossible to finish in middle of line at end of page except by extending letters — not practiced here in Baghdad; rather they extend letters and finish at end of page and in middle of line; and see our words Yoreh Deah siman 272 letters 11 and 13; and see above letter 7.
kol-yaakov/9:_: (ט) There regarding hekef gvil, etc. — chet invalid for all — Knesset HaGedolah end of siman; and so Acharonim; and so Magen Tzvi; and even in minority invalid like Torah scroll; and Peri Chadash letter 2 wrote: if majority written validly do not invalidate it; and so Levush in Hagahot Magen Avraham there s.k. 1; and see Birkei Yosef letter 2.
levushei-serad/10:_: s.k. 6 if he has megillah lest you say already written so — it would be b'dieved; and he said: fix for certain must fix except in time of duress and no leisure to fix immediately — this is b'dieved.
levushei-serad/1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 1 first line, etc. So too Bach; but Darkei Moshe challenged: since we say requires scoring like Torah itself — if so entire column requires scoring like Torah scroll; and perhaps Magen Avraham did not see Darkei Moshe's words.
levushei-serad/3:_: Shulchan Aruch seif 2: requires a pole at its end, etc. Meaning: leave parchment folded to roll over a wooden pole the megillah rolls on; at its head leave a large part to roll all its circumference since a megillah has not two poles to roll to middle as in Torah scroll but one pole and rolls from end to beginning.
levushei-serad/6:_: s.k. 2 that there is dispute. Tur brings many poskim wrote opposite — pole at head and section at end and roll from head to end; therefore better sit and do not act and do not make a pole at all; and if so also do not make a section — from this reasoning itself there is dispute; and I already wrote at beginning (on Mechaber's words seif 2) they make a section — one can say section is required to leave as cover for megillah circumference from honor of holy writings; world relies on this view that section at head; and if they rely on this view because section is required — if so they should also make pole at end. And one can say specifically when there is section and pole the great ones disputed which is better at head or end; but where only section with no pole there is no stringency at all — where done, done.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: (s.k. 1) like Torah itself, etc. siman 32, etc. Levush wrote as Orach Chayyim wrote and Darkei Moshe wrote on it: we do not practice thus, etc. — as gemara says: words of peace and truth teach requires scoring like truth of Torah. Commentators divided on truth of Torah — if Torah scroll or mezuzah. They learned from there requires scoring all lines, etc.; therefore wonder on Levush who brought Orach Chayyim anonymously without dispute when whole world disputes. Explanation of Rabbenu Tam: holds Torah scroll does not require scoring — rather as we say in Gittin 6b: three words forbidden to write without scoring — must be in Torah scroll it does not require scoring all lines — enough if he scores top line; and mezuzah though they said no scoring — nevertheless top line needs scoring. And what we say megillah requires scoring like truth of Torah — not Torah scroll he says no scoring required but like mezuzah requiring scoring all lines; other poskim dispute and hold also Torah scroll must score all lines; if so what we say like truth of Torah means Torah scroll. In any case for all megillah requires scoring all lines (and see Rosh Laws of Torah scroll and Megillah ch. 2 and Tosafot Gittin 6b and chapter HaKometz). Magen Avraham pointed to see siman 32 explained there: though tefillin need no scoring nevertheless must score top line; if so megillah which requires scoring — perforce all lines. Also per this Levush's words contradict each other.
machatzit-hashekel/8:_: (s.k. 8) in congregation, etc. and every ten, etc. — to exclude poskim Tur brought who hold specifically in synagogue is called congregation for this matter since there is primary publicizing of miracle.
magen-avraham/5:_: Open [parashiyot] invalid. Rama's responsum siman 12 law 5 doubts this; therefore it appears to rely in time of duress — see siman 649 seif 3.
magen-avraham/9:_: Blessings and piyyutim. And one could say to write between the Writings — there it is not recognizable it is megillah unlike here (Rashba siman 150) (and in Tashbetz siman 223 wrote his blessings should not be written in it l'chatchila); and so Hagahot Maimoniot and Mordekhai and Levush.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (ח) Regarding surrounding hide — on every letter. The same for everything; therefore we require its lines be equal; also column width "for your families" and all Torah scroll laws.
peri-megadim/1:_: In afatzim water, etc. — his intent from Gittin 12a: they wrote a get in mei milin and afatz — valid; and Tosafot there and Hagahot Ashiri: at first glance afatz is not Mishnah ink; they answered when mixed, etc.; and Taz wrote on what Rama said: one can say afatz is chibur — ground gallnuts kneaded in water writing with it — not included in ink; but mei sheriyat afatzin or kneaded is ink; and the word with beit seems should be without — Magen Avraham did not bring Kol Mefareish. And know Shulchan Aruch brought Rambam ch. 2 Megillah halacha 9 specifically on gvil and klaf — not on duchsustos; and in Laws of Torah scroll Rambam invalidates Torah scroll on duchsustos; and Yoreh Deah siman 271 seif 3 wrote on gvil and klaf and did not finish if duchsustos invalidates Torah scroll; and in Mishnah it says on paper and hide invalid — implies duchsustos since paper is not valid; nevertheless ch. 2 Megillah see our master no processing lishmah required; and what not mentioned equal lines for megillah — from where; and per this on klaf and gvil not duchsustos; and from that it should be written on the scroll — specifically gvil and klaf — from where implied; and in Hagahot letter 30 in name of Semag proof megillah written among Writings individual fulfills — see there implies written with them one processing; and so Bach in name of Semag; Bach wrote see Tur; and Rabbenu Tam wrote R' Hai does not disagree what preceded; and one can say from Mishnah stam on paper invalid implies duchsustos valid; and Rabbenu Tam wrote to say it has all Torah scroll law — if so per those who invalidate duchsustos in Torah scroll — same megillah; see Tur. Rosh validates all in Torah scroll; and it appears l'chatchila not to write megillah on duchsustos and same Torah scroll per Rambam; and so Magen Avraham will explain further.
peri-megadim/2:א: (א) Also afatz, etc. and I did not understand — behold they leave section for its circumference at head; and as there is dispute on pole (wood they attach at head or end) or head or end — so dispute on section; since so — should leave section at head and end; and further they act and roll from end to head; also possible to satisfy both views — pole at head and end; and what he wrote in name of Rashba explained siman 690 Magen Avraham letter 15: listener must hear every word — only listener need not intend each word — see there; and there I wondered on responsum language — here cannot extend.
peri-megadim/2:ב: (ב) Behold Mechaber wrote requires surrounding hide each letter surrounded and tagin on chet two zayins, etc., and hanging of hei and kuf — all like Torah scroll per Rabbenu Tam alone except what is noted in commentary not equal to Torah scroll; and if to tag — also gimel tzadi hei brought two views; and from processing no difficulty — proof from megillah among Writings as said; and in Bach see Tur and Hagahot Maimoniot wrote need not tag it — meaning unlike Rabbenu Tam; perhaps his intent tagin too are Torah scroll laws — only what noted in commentary equal to Torah scroll; difficult here; and as I wrote; also tagin on chet — in Torah scroll scribes are not accustomed to tagin; all the more megillah; and siman 32 that scribes were exact wrote tagin — not other scribes (and there is somewhat proof from what is written not to make hei like chet); and Yoreh Deah 274 used tagin in Tur and Shulchan Aruch tagin; Magen Avraham siman 36 letter 3.
peri-megadim/2:ג: (ג) Further I will tell you Yoreh Deah 281 seif 3 and four: Torah scroll — worker and woman and minor invalid — learned from tefillin — see there; in megillah woman and eved are obligated at least in hearing — may write; but minor though reached chinuch — not like adult as explained siman 689 invalid to write. And mamzer and ger — some invalidate writing Torah scroll; and Shach there letter 8 reason in name of Mordekhai: mamzer does not discharge many — invalid to write — and perforce same megillah; and it appears write one who can discharge in performance. And know Mordekhai: mamzer does not discharge many — wonder in my eyes — mamzer is full Israel and obligated in the matter; to say pesulei kahal not in areivut except kosher — same Egyptian and Edomite (however paragraph — no lack from soul side; see Taz Rosh Hashanah nowadays discharges from areivut — if so can settle this; requires study — did not find any posek this; see above siman 353 and 355 mamzer to be shaliach tzibbur — see there; also listener like answerer). And know Shach Yoreh Deah there wrote reason mamzer and ger not obligated in all mitzvot therefore invalid — see there; and this is mamzer permitted with shifchah and am ha'aretz siman 4 and Beit Shmuel there; and ger permitted with mamzeret and Egyptian and Edomite (but not fit to be king and judge in chalitzah — if so blind in one eye also invalid for Torah scroll) but in Shulchan Aruch there ger toshav — accepted not to worship idolatry with partnership; partnership I explained in Pri Yoreh Deah — implies stam ger tzedek valid for Torah scroll; if so Taz there letter 4 mamzer valid for megillah; and Mordekhai invalid; Magen Avraham 39 letter 9 in name of Darkei Moshe mamzer and ger toshav valid for tefillin — difficult behold writing requires lishmah in tefillin how validated; Magen Avraham 32; in Florence Darkei Moshe word toshav omitted — see there. Again the Holy One blessed be He enlightened my eyes — I examined Mordekhai Krakow edition end Bava Kamma 56 (in some editions error — see lower number there 7 8) brought Sifrei Soferim: ger stam — Mordekhai per his method explains ger toshav; but for reason does not discharge many as Mordekhai there in name of Rabbenu Simcha: no mamzer — in Torah scroll whoever discharges many writes it and mamzer discharges — Mordekhai reads mamzer and learns mamzer does not discharge many or mah or midrash — and perforce same ger tzedek per Rosh Berachot women not in areivut — see there 21b; also per Shach's reason ger tzedek; in Mishneh Torah reads stam ger as I wrote; and see siman 39 and 353 and 355 — requires study.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Siman 691 Magen Avraham s.k. 1 however enough with scoring. I wonder — this is in tefillin that need no scoring; and in Torah scroll for those who hold no scoring — nevertheless must score first line to straighten writing; but in mezuzah requiring scoring — must every line; and perforce same megillah since we say requires scoring like truth of Torah.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: (•) Seif 1 in Shulchan Aruch: one does not write, etc. — see Eliyah Rabbah who brought in name of Maharam Provencial in responsum manuscript: incident they printed megillot on (parchment) and required burial as invalid because engraved impression — lest come to validate them; but on paper will not err — see there; and see Peri Chadash: if majority printed invalid but majority written valid — unlike Sefer Hazichronot, etc.; and see Sefer Korban Netanel who challenged him comparing to scribe omission, etc. — this written improperly detracts as Rashi 9a and Eliyah Rabbah defended Peri Chadash that Tosafot argue Rashi — see there. Regarding printing if engraved impression — several responsa treat as writing — see above siman 484 and Yoreh Deah Laws of Torah scroll; and see Tashbetz part 1 siman 8 megillah written mashit (like our blot) invalid — brought in Knesset HaGedolah; wondered on poskim (who omitted) from our Mishnah taught until written Assyrian — see there; I shortened here: (א) scoring — Avodat Yisrael; and what he wrote in name of Chavot Yair Eliyah Rabbah Knesset HaGedolah wrote room for God's word returns after entirely scored; nevertheless first line scored b'dieved valid; if not scored at all invalid even b'dieved.
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: Surrounding. And see Eliyah Rabbah in name of Keter Kehuna manuscript: all that the hide has to write three pages — even if only one page written valid b'dieved in Torah scroll — all the more megillah — see there; and Yoreh Deah siman 271; and see Sanhedrin 21 when they came to Esther megillah they said it does not require a cloth — see there; and Moed Katan wrote requires cloth — plain on page 21 see there; and in truth Talmud is opposite — only in She'elat Ya'avetz wrote difficult: why said does not require since it defiles hands — main reason defilement of hands lest they handle naked without cloth; perhaps therefore R' Yehudah strict to say it does not exist but requires cloth — see there; custom is not like his words and not careful at all to take megillah without cloth — and plainly Talmud words: since called iggeret without cloth suffices; and though called sefer — for matters that are validity of writing such as scoring and surrounding hide; but matters after writing like iggeret; and even though defiles hands — taken naked like tefillin; see Magen Avraham siman 147 his view to be careful megillah written properly; Peri Megadim part 1 siman 76 wrote world not careful; brought there from Talmud Sanhedrin; and Shulchan Aruch Berachot siman 11 his view to permit even megillah — see there he wrote therefore two poles in Torah scroll because forbidden to hold naked unlike holy writings — see there; see Eliyah Rabbah siman 147 explains Hagahah there; good to be strict if did not wash hands standing on megillah; even stam hands; known soiled hands strict even other holy writings — see there; world not careful to take stam hands before taking megillah in hand; good to be strict as Eliyah Rabbah.
shaarei-teshuvah/7:_: Page. Avodat Yisrael; and see responsa Beit Ephraim siman 72 at length on this and on what is practiced to write ten sons of Haman in large letters — see there explained also prevent l'chatchila writing hint of Holy Name in abbreviation or Torah scroll large letters — see there in Shaarei Ephraim and Pitchei Shearim; see there in name of Machazit Hashekel who wrote in name of Zera Emet megillah if not written on last page only three or four lines and did not finish at page end and did not finish mid-line — valid l'chatchila — see there; see Eliyah Rabbah in name of Maharam if megillah written out of order he does not fulfill; Maharash Halevi wavers on the matter.
turei-zahav/1:_: In afatzim water and kankantom. Explanation: mei kankantom — but kankantom itself invalid as in Mishnah; and so Tur kankantom invalid; and same here; and this is his language: know in kankantom invalid and in its water valid; and in ch. 1 Rambam wrote: if he wrote Torah scroll tefillin mezuzot in afatzim water and kankantom — valid; and wrote in Kol Mefareish: though in Gittin implies afatz water is not Mishnah ink when mixed with gum called in foreign language goma — called ink — end; and I wonder he did not bring Kol Mefareish.
turei-zahav/2:_: Also practiced not to make a pole. Reason appears dispute among early ones whether pole at head or end — therefore practiced not to make pole at all. Rashba wrote in responsum siman 567: reader of megillah to discharge congregation — even if he omitted only one word returns, etc. — implies Yerushalmi in error that Jews there language and matter one — he does not return; if not so he returns; but for listeners need not intend each word — he brought proofs.
yad-ephraim/2:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 4: megillah forbidden to write by heart, etc. as Darkei Moshe in name of Ran; but requires study why he brought this in name of Ran — it is Arukh on 18a; and implies there even in duress specifically like R' Meir who had them before him; and Ran stated matter in name of Yerushalmi permitted in duress; requires study — perhaps Yerushalmi too means our Talmud there on even expert like Ezra; also why not write in Shulchan Aruch R' Yehudah's extension that even one letter forbidden not from written copy; see above siman 32 s.k. 42 who answered divide tefillin where reads verses and see what is written there in Yad Ephraim and Magen Avraham here; and even if dealing after, etc. — meaning what is written to utter every word does not refer to what was written initially must write from written copy.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And it requires ruled lines. On every line — unlike Levush and Magen Avraham; they erred, for regarding tefillin that do not require ruled lines we say thus as in Tosafot Gittin 6b on the matter beginning R' Yitzchak said etc.; and if you say etc.; and Rabbenu Tam says etc.; and likewise in Agudah; but mezuzah and anything that requires ruled lines perforce we require on every line; and see there and in Rosh.
beur-hagra/6:א: (א) Seif 6 — and because it has various explanations. Rashi and Tosafot explained one [stitch] in its middle and two in its fourth parts; proof from what is written in Makkot 9 that three must be plaited etc.; and Rif explained two at the corners, proof from what is written in Eruvin 57 three villages that are triangular etc.; and likewise in Bechorot 38 regarding blemishes; and see chapter HaAreil, chapter there; and likewise Rambam explained, except he explained three threads in every stitch like a triangular heifer and triangular goat etc.; and see there in Targum; and see in Rosh there and in Tosafot and in Tosafot Bechorot 39a s.v. sheyehu etc.
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Mechaber seif 1 NB see Sanhedrin daf 100a that megillah does not require a cloth. However Mahariatz vol. 2 s.k. 173 raised that per our understanding megillah was said in ruach hakodesh to read and to write — forbidden to touch it naked and it requires a cloth — see there. And I saw my teacher ztz"l that at time of reading he was careful not to touch it naked; and still requires study in Magen Avraham siman 147 s.k. 1 and requires study in Radbaz vol. 2 siman 391.
